title: Montague Chelmsford Reforms 1919
definition: The Government of India Act 1919, based on the Montague-Chelmsford Report, was a legislative measure to increase Indian participation in the administration by introducing 'Dyarchy' in provinces and expanding the central legislature.
importanceInUpsc: It is a cornerstone of Constitutional History, frequently tested for its structural changes, the introduction of Dyarchy, and its role in the transition from the 1909 Morley-Minto reforms to the 1935 Act.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Montague Chelmsford Reforms 1919.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
